Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Norman OK
607 AM CDT Thu Aug 27 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...
Updated at 516 AM CDT Thu Aug 27 2026

- A few storms possible across the west today.

- Less hot weather is expected through today.

- Hot and dry conditions return this weekend and continue next
  week.

&&

.NEAR TERM...
(Through Thursday)
Issued at 124 AM CDT Thu Aug 27 2026

A complex of storms moving across the northwest Oklahoma and Texas 
panhandles will continue to drift east and southeast early this 
morning. This activity will likely hold together long enough to 
enter western portions of Oklahoma late tonight and linger into the 
morning hours Thursday. There is a low chance that some light 
showers may linger through the middle part of the day before daytime 
heating allows for a few additional thunderstorms to develop during 
the afternoon. This would likely be confined to southwest Oklahoma 
and western north Texas. The strongest may be capable of some gusty 
winds. 

Otherwise, another "cooler" day today as again most of the area will 
remain in the 90s for afternoon highs. A few locations near the Red 
River, southward into north Texas may see temperatures around 100 
degrees, although lingering cloud cover may have something to say 
about that potential. 

&&

.SHORT TERM...
(Thursday night through Saturday night)
Issued at 124 AM CDT Thu Aug 27 2026

Overnight tonight another complex of storms is expected across the 
central Plains that will move south toward northern Oklahoma during 
the early morning hours. Quite a range of solutions during this time 
frame, with some models having nothing to others that bring 
lingering convection into northern Oklahoma before sunrise, with yet 
others holding off until later in the day Friday. 

With the anticipated expansion of the upper ridge back eastward 
across the southern Plains overnight into Friday, will hold off on 
any mention of precip at this point, but will be something to 
monitor.

Otherwise, temperatures will begin to respond to the building upper 
ridge overhead and warm back into the mid/upper 90s and low 100s 
Friday afternoon. This eastward expansion will continue over the 
weekend with a gradual warming trend occurring. Little to no 
chance of precip during this time as well.

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Sunday through Wednesday)
Issued at 124 AM CDT Thu Aug 27 2026

By Sunday, most locations will once again see highs in the triple 
digits as the center of the upper ridge settles overhead. Sunday may 
also see the return of heat related headlines. Low level 
temperatures do not warm as much as the last couple of weeks, so 
even though the area will see triple digit highs, currently do not 
anticipate the extreme temperatures that were seen this last week. 
In addition, the upper ridge continues to translate eastward, so by 
early next week the center of the ridge moves toward the eastern 
part of the country. Unfortunately, the ridge will continue to have 
just enough influence over the southern Plains to keep most of the 
area hot and dry. One exception may be northwest Oklahoma, where 
proximity to the southwest flow may allow a few showers/storms to 
occur.

Winds are expected to increase as well Sunday and Monday as a trough 
sets up across the west with embedded shortwaves ejecting out of the 
southwest into the central and northern Plains. This will cause lee 
surface trough to develop aiding in increasing pressure gradient 
through the Plains. By Tuesday, the upper ridge once again expands 
through the central and southern Plains, which will push any 
shortwave troughs farther north away from the area, which should 
allow winds to relax to some degree. This will also limit any 
possibility of precip during this time frame.

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 516 AM CDT Thu Aug 27 2026

VFR conditions to continue.

An area of showers and storms moving into western Oklahoma this
morning may impact WWR/CSM for a couple of hours before
dissipating. Otherwise, widespread mid and upper clouds expected
through much of the day. There is a chance for a few isolated
storms across southwest OK and western north TX this afternoon,
but chances remain too low to include at this time. Skies are
expected to gradually clear late this afternoon and this evening.  
Light northeast winds today will become more easterly overnight. 

&&

.PRELIMINARY POINT TEMPS/POPS...
Oklahoma City OK  94  71  96  72 /  10   0   0   0 
Hobart OK         96  70  98  72 /  20   0   0   0 
Wichita Falls TX 100  71 101  73 /  20   0   0   0 
Gage OK           92  66  96  70 /  50  10  10   0 
Ponca City OK     94  69  94  71 /   0  10  10   0 
Durant OK         99  72  99  71 /  10   0  10   0 

&&

.OUN WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
OK...None.
TX...None.
&&

$$

NEAR TERM...30
SHORT TERM...30
LONG TERM....30
AVIATION...30
